validity.recommendation: Real, correctly-classified national-grid gas trunk segment, but rests on ONE Arabic press source (not the 2-independent near-requirement) and that source only shows the project 'under implementation' as of Jan 2021, not a confirmed operational date. Seek a second source (GASCO/EGAS annual report, EIB/industry project ledger) to (a) corroborate existence independently of the sheet's own cited Youm7 article and (b) pin down the actual completion/start date, which may be later than 2021.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's only existing citation for this row (per wiki_citations.json) is a single Youm7 (اليوم السابع) article dated 2021-01-21, 'Details of national natural gas network projects currently being implemented' (تفاصيل مشروعات الشبكة القومية للطبيعية الجارى تنفيذها). Item 6 of that article reads verbatim: 'خط إزدواج دمياط / فيونسا بطول 12 كم - قطر 42" تكلفة المشروع : 340 مليون جنيه' (Damietta/Fyonsa duplication line, 12 km, 42in diameter, cost 340M EGP) — this EXACTLY matches GEM's current Length=12.00km and Diameter=42in, confirming GEM's own data was drawn from this article and is not fabricated. 'Fyonsa' (فيونسا, spelling variant of فينوسا/Fenosa) is confirmed via a separate presidency.eg release on the related Gamasa-Fenosa line (P6035) to refer to Union Fenosa Gas / SEGAS's intake chamber ('فينوسا' + 'ايميثانيكس' = the Fenosa AND Egyptian-Methanex intake room) in the New Damietta industrial zone — this validates GEM's 'SEGAS' naming as a reasonable English gloss of the same facility, not an invented endpoint. EXISTENCE: no fabrication evident, but only ONE distinct source names this specific 12km/42in project; extensive search (Youm7 archive, presidency.eg, petro-news.com's separate 39-project roundup, egy-map.com, GASCO/EGAS sites, general Arabic search) turned up no second independent confirmation of this exact project (the 39-project roundup's Damietta-area 'duplication' entry is a DIFFERENT project — Edko–Abu Hummus, 30km/42in/733M EGP — not this one). Tier = medium, independent = false. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a national-grid gas transmission duplication/loop segment (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission both consistent with the source's framing as part of 'الشبكة القومية للطبيعية' — the national gas grid); not gathering/plant-internal. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 30-row Egypt-gas-operating roster and the GulfPub Egypt gas list — no other row matches len=12km/dia=42in near Damietta. Confirmed NOT a duplicate of the similarly 'Fenosa'-linked P6035 Gamasa–Veunsa Gas Pipeline (34km/42in, feeds the West Damietta power station per presidency.eg + petro-news.com, completed per egy-map.com as far back as Oct 2015) — those are two distinct pipe segments feeding the same general Fenosa/SEGAS/Methanex Damietta industrial node from different directions/dates; also not the same as P6037 Al Gamil–Damietta (50km/42in, different route) or GulfPub's Idku–Damietta (103km/32in) / Damietta–Port Said (112km/32in) / Ha'py–Damietta (38km/16in) records. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) 100% is defensible — GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company), the entity that actually builds/operates Egypt's national gas grid pipelines including compressor-station contracts named elsewhere in this same Youm7 article, is a wholly-owned EGAS subsidiary — but no source explicitly names an owner for THIS specific segment, so I did not add an Owner ref (left unresolved rather than fabricated). Start/End both = 'Damietta' (flagged 'irregular' in the worklist) is plausible, not necessarily an error: this is a short local 'duplication' (إزدواج = doubling/looping an existing pipe) inside the Damietta/New Damietta industrial zone rather than a route between two distinct cities — see routes[] for a proposed real-endpoint refinement. SPEC: Length (12.00km) and Diameter (42in) both match the source exactly — confirmed, tier medium. StartYear1=2021 is weaker: the source only shows the project as 'currently being implemented' (الجارى تنفيذها) as of Jan 2021, with no stated completion date for this specific item (unlike some sibling items in the same article that DO list a completion month) — 2021 is a plausible but not confirmed start year; it is at least contextually consistent with SEGAS LNG's own documented Q1/Feb-2021 restart after its 2012–2021 shutdown (per SEGAS LNG / en.wikipedia.org), which would have driven exactly this kind of local supply-reinforcement project, but that is circumstantial, not a direct second source. Capacity is blank in the sheet and no source gives a throughput figure (only cost) — correctly left unfilled, not forced.

routes.start_name: National gas-grid take-off point, New Damietta industrial zone, Damietta Governorate, Egypt (exact node/station not named in the available source)
routes.end_name: SEGAS LNG plant / Union Fenosa Gas (فيونسا) gas intake & metering station, New Damietta, Damietta Governorate, Egypt
routes.corridor_desc: GEM's sheet records identical Start and End location values ('Damietta'/'Damietta'), consistent with this being a short ~12km 'duplication' (إزدواج, i.e. a parallel/looping pipe added alongside an existing line to add capacity) entirely within the New Damietta industrial zone, rather than a route between two distinct named cities. The one named, coordinate-sourced anchor is the SEGAS LNG / Union Fenosa Gas intake and metering chamber (also serving the adjacent Egyptian Methanex methanol plant) at approx. 31.4677N, 31.7691E (Wikidata Q7389666; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SEGAS_LNG and offshore-technology.com, which place the complex in New Damietta ~60km west of Port Said). The other end — the actual take-off point on the existing national grid that this line duplicates/parallels — is not named in the available source; by analogy with the related Gamasa–Fenosa line (P6035), which taps 'room 10 on the Idku–Damietta 32in line' before reaching the same Fenosa/Methanex intake chamber, this duplication line likely originates from a nearby metering/take-off point on the existing Damietta-area grid (Idku–Damietta corridor or a GASCO reduction station in/near New Damietta), but that specific node is NOT independently confirmed for THIS project and is not asserted as fact. Treat the corridor as bounded to a several-km radius around the SEGAS/Methanex industrial complex in New Damietta until a human sources the exact take-off point.
routes.researcher_notes: Coordinates for the SEGAS LNG / Fenosa intake endpoint are taken directly from Wikidata's sourced coordinate field (31°28'3.868"N, 31°46'8.695"E → 31.4677, 31.7691), a real, defensible location for a named facility — not invented. The opposite (start) endpoint's exact coordinates are deliberately left null because no source names the specific take-off point for this particular duplication segment; describing it in words instead of guessing coordinates, per standing rules against fabricating coordinates.

summary: P6033 (Damietta–SEGAS Pipeline) is a real, correctly-classified 12km/42in national-grid gas duplication line whose Length/Diameter/Fuel/PipelineType/Location match its single existing Youm7 (2021) source exactly, but corroboration is single-source only (no independent 2nd source found) and the StartYear=2021 is unconfirmed (source shows 'in progress', not completed) — verdict confirmed (caveat)/spec, not a duplicate of the similarly Fenosa-linked P6035 (Gamasa–Veunsa, 34km, different project). Proposed a low-confidence route: end anchored at SEGAS LNG's sourced coordinates (31.4677, 31.7691); start left unsourced/null rather than fabricated.
